This app is a reporting and visualisation tool.

A photo-based pollution index describes visible river conditions only. It cannot replace a laboratory water test, does not establish compliance with an effluent standard, and is not a substitute for the official complaint channel.

Use a gateway token (st:…) issued by your own proxy gateway. The real model key never leaves the server, so unpacking the APK reveals nothing usable. Without a credential the app still works — every photo is analysed by the on-device engine.

Encrypted with an Android Keystore AES-GCM key before it touches disk, and sent only to the gateway you configure. This does not defend against a memory dump on a live device, but it does stop plain-text leaks through file copies, backups or adb.

A downscaled copy of the photo (longest side 1280 px) plus a fixed instruction prompt. No account name, phone number or precise address is included. Every result screen shows whether the answer came from the on-device engine, the gateway or a direct call.

The authority that receives pollution reports and issues enforcement action in Malaysia.
Why doesn\'t the app report an "exceedance ratio"?

A photograph cannot measure dissolved oxygen, ammonia nitrogen or heavy metals, so any "exceedance ratio" derived from an image is pseudo-quantitative. This app only produces a visual anomaly index that is independent of any standard; a legally valid conclusion requires on-site sampling by an accredited laboratory.

Ranking counts "valid findings": severity R2 or above, approved by review, and only once per water body per 24 hours. Anonymous reports, rejected reports and R0/R1 records do not score. Newcomers with fewer than 5 valid findings are kept off the board so their identity cannot be inferred.

This app is a photo-based tool for collecting and visualising pollution leads. It is not a laboratory test and is not an official complaint channel. Results are a visual lead score and must not be used as evidence of an offence; the authority decides whether pollution occurred and how it is handled.
